items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Freddy had made good in Paris as an orchestra leader and wanted me to join him.

ctx.x: But in August I received a letter from Freddy Taylor whom I had given a beat-up trumpet when I left Paris, France. Freddy had stayed in France but was now back in New York looking for some musicians to take back to France. He had asked for me especially and had gotten my address in Cincinnati from someone in New York and sent me a letter saying that he had made good in Paris as an orchestra leader and wanted me to join him. I had bigger eyes for going back to Europe than I did for getting a divorce and I figured…

So I jumped at the idea and sent Freddy a telegram saying that I would accept his offer and later sent him a letter in which I explained why I was in Cincinnati and told him not to say anything to anyone, even the other musicians he had engaged whom I did not know who they would be. I knew that if the word got around that I was going to Europe, it would get to Madelyn and that would have been the end of that. New York is a very big city with millions of people, but if you are known in a certain circle, the grape…

But sometimes there is a possibility of a secret being kept, and there is a certain honour among thieves considering what circumstances may be. So the word did not get on that I was going to France. Beezie and I arrived in New York around 10th of September 1935 and went straight to Leonia, New Jersey and stayed with her step-father.
